name: Improper Access Control
principle: The product does not restrict, or incorrectly restricts, an unauthorized actor's access to a resource. Failed authentication, authorization, privilege, ownership, or accountability checks can allow privilege gain, sensitive data access, command execution, or evasion of detection.
detection_signals: controller/handler reads request parameter id/userId/accountId and calls findById/load/get without accessControl.check(currentUser, resource)
Spring @GetMapping/@PostMapping/@DeleteMapping on non-public endpoint without @PreAuthorize/@Secured or explicit server-side authorization call
authorization decision uses client-controlled request parameter/cookie/header such as role=isAdmin, userId, group, permission
C/C++ chmod(path, 0777) or chmod(path, 0666) on sensitive file or directory
Java Files.setPosixFilePermissions includes OTHERS_WRITE or OTHERS_READ on sensitive resource
privilege elevation call setuid(0)/seteuid(0)/setreuid(...,0) followed by sensitive operation without guaranteed drop in cleanup/finally/RAII
CORS response sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true for authenticated API
negative_signals: resource access is preceded by server-side accessControl.check(authenticatedUser, action, resource) and denial returns 403
database query scopes resource by authenticated principal, e.g. WHERE id=? AND owner_id=?
endpoint has @PreAuthorize/@Secured with role and object-level permission expression before business logic
ACL/permission parser fails closed on missing, malformed, or unknown rule
privilege elevation is wrapped with try/finally or RAII cleanup that always drops privileges
public/static resource is explicitly annotated or routed as public and contains no sensitive operation
false_defense_traps: client-side UI hiding, JavaScript checks, hidden fields, or disabled buttons without server-side authorization
authentication-only checks such as isLoggedIn() for object-specific or role-specific operations
trusting JWT/cookie/header role claims without signature verification and server-side policy evaluation
blacklisting a few admin URLs while default route behavior allows access
dropping privileges only on the success path after a call that can throw or return early
verification_focus: Does trusted server-side code enforce the intended access policy for this actor, action, and resource on every path?

consequence_chains.trigger: unauthorized actor can read a protected resource
access control grants or retains excessive privileges
consequence_chains.consequence: privilege escalation or execution of privileged actions

consequence_chains.trigger: dangerous method or function is exposed to an unauthorized caller
consequence_chains.consequence: unauthorized command, configuration, or state change

patch_principle: Enforce authorization in trusted server-side code before every sensitive operation.
Use default-deny and least-privilege policies; explicitly mark only intended public resources.
Bind resource access to ownership, role, tenant, and action checks instead of trusting client identifiers.
Manage privilege changes with fail-closed error handling and guaranteed privilege drop.
Compartmentalize trust zones and keep sensitive data inside the intended boundary.
